description: Somos el equipo de los michis espaciales, nuestras habilidades son la creación de videojuegos y animación
summary: What if a child could design the space mission that helps save a city? That’s the idea behind Mission: Otis Night, an educational video game built in Godot for elementary school kids. It’s inspired by Hurricane Otis, which became a Category 5 in just hours in 2023 and struck Acapulco. The game has two modes. In Story Mode, a crew of explorer cats explains what a space mission is and how NASA satellites watched Otis grow, using real images and data. In Game Mode, kids build their spacecraft, choose their role and plan the mission through minigames, managing power, budget and time just like real engineers. That’s how we meet the challenge: kids design their own mission in a simple, fun way. It matters because it turns a disaster many know about into a lesson of hope: space science protects lives, and any of them can be part of it.
details:
In October 2023, Hurricane Otis went from a tropical storm to a Category 5 in less than a day and caught Acapulco by surprise. Mission: Otis Night starts from that real story to teach elementary school kids something powerful: we protect life on Earth from space, too.

In Story Mode, kids discover what a space mission is and how NASA satellites tracked Otis. In Game Mode, they become space engineers: they build their own spacecraft, choose their role and plan their mission through minigames, managing power, budget and time just like a real mission. Every decision counts.

We want every child who plays it to realize that science isn’t far from their lives, that it can help their community, and that someday they could design the mission that saves lives. It’s a way to inspire Mexico’s future scientists and engineers.

We built it in Godot with GDScript, using real NASA images and data (Earth Observatory, Worldview and the GPM mission).

What makes it unique is that it connects a disaster many Mexican kids lived through or heard about with the excitement of designing a space mission, guided by a crew of explorer cats that makes learning fun and relatable.

As a team, we made sure it was easy for kids to understand, based on a real problem in Mexico, and built on real NASA information, so kids learn from real data and not just fantasy.
